description: Dispatch an async job that merges up to 25 losing leads into one winning lead, and return {job_id, status} in milliseconds; poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished success and request_id. Writable fields follow Marketo's general precedence: the winner's value wins when present, while a losing value may fill a null winner. Read-only fields are an observed exception: they keep the winning record's value, including an empty one, and are never populated from a losing record, although Adobe's general precedence documentation predicts otherwise. merge_in_crm additionally merges natively-synced CRM records, capping losing_lead_ids at 1. Destructive write action.
embedding_description: Merge duplicate Marketo lead/person records so one winner absorbs losing records' history, memberships, and eligible field values. Read-only fields keep the winning record's value, including an empty one, and are never populated from a losing record; Adobe's documented general precedence rule predicts the opposite. Up to 25 losing leads are supported, or one with merge_in_crm.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with job_id (pass to check_marketo_job_status) and status 'queued'. The completed job result is a dict with success (bool) and request_id.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: A queued job is not a completed merge: give the job_id and poll check_marketo_job_status. Once completed, this destructive, irreversible action must be confirmed clearly — name the winning_lead_id and how many losing leads were absorbed; there is no undo.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Never say the leads were merged from THIS verb's response -- it carries only the job handle. The merge is confirmed only once check_marketo_job_status reports status=completed with success=true.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validate a lead merge and dispatch a background job that merges the losing leads into the winning lead in the configured Marketo instance.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: Refused at dispatch, before any vendor call and with no job created: marketo.invalid_params for missing winning_lead_id/losing_lead_ids, more than 25 losing_lead_ids (or more than 1 when merge_in_crm=true), a non-boolean merge_in_crm, or missing session_id/flow_id in the calling context. Reported later in check_marketo_job_status's error field: marketo.invalid_params for Marketo's own over-cap code 1080. marketo.validation_failed: Marketo couldn't determine a default record type for the merge (code 714) or the winner/losers are otherwise incompatible. marketo.object_not_found: a lead id in the request doesn't exist. marketo.not_configured: no marketo_instance address-book entry. marketo.permission_denied: the API user's Role lacks Read-Write Person — this write permission is NOT checked by check_setup (unverifiable without performing a write), so this may be the FIRST signal of the gap. A transport fault after dispatch may follow a vendor mutation.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: marketo.invalid_params: reduce losing_lead_ids to the applicable cap (25, or 1 with merge_in_crm). marketo.object_not_found: confirm every lead id via get_leads first. marketo.permission_denied: add 'Read-Write Person' under Admin > Users & Roles > Roles > <the API role> > Access API, then retry. After a transport fault, read the leads back with get_leads before retrying: a merge that already happened cannot be repeated.
